nodes.label: Accepted Eventual-Consistency Windows (settings 60 s, AI status, SWR)
nodes.norm_label: accepted eventual-consistency windows (settings 60 s, ai status, swr)
nodes.rationale: A second tab may lag a target change up to 60 s per process and quota display may lag one request; acceptable for a single-user preference tracker.

nodes.label: Decision: No Shared/CDN Caching Anywhere
nodes.rationale: Every workspace payload is personalized per account, so nothing user-specific may be shared; adding revalidate, unstable_cache or cache tags requires a documented per-source policy change here first.

nodes.label: Decision: App Client Does Not Consume SWR Windows
nodes.norm_label: decision: app client does not consume swr windows
nodes.rationale: Charts must reflect the last save immediately, so correctness-first freshness beats the speed gain scripts would get from raising max-age/stale-while-revalidate.

nodes.label: Decision: Server Cache Limited to the Settings LRU
nodes.norm_label: decision: server cache limited to the settings lru
nodes.rationale: Settings is the only read-hot, rarely-changing, write-through-invalidatable store; attempt data changes through user mutations that must be visible on the next request.

nodes.label: Decision: Retry neon init with --agent codex
nodes.norm_label: decision: retry neon init with --agent codex
nodes.rationale: The GitHub Copilot plugin installer failed, so initialization was retried with an explicit agent target to complete the required Codex setup without depending on the unrelated failed installer.

nodes.label: package-lock-only Install Blocked by Remote-Package Policy
nodes.norm_label: package-lock-only install blocked by remote-package policy
nodes.rationale: Rather than disable the machine's remote-package policy, the lockfile install-script flag was synchronized locally because dependency install and audit had already succeeded.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Identity Is a Hard Constraint for the Overhaul
nodes.norm_label: design.md identity is a hard constraint for the overhaul
nodes.rationale: Warm paper, serif headlines, thin rules, semantic chart palette, animation off and data-table twins must survive the overhaul, so visual changes stay tokenized rather than re-theming the product.

nodes.label: User's 'Moderately Rounded Corners' Directive Honored via Tokens
nodes.norm_label: user's 'moderately rounded corners' directive honored via tokens
nodes.rationale: Roundedness is applied as a tokenized radius scale on controls and already-rounded surfaces only, not by rounding the dashboard's structural geometry, to avoid breaking the DESIGN.md identity.

nodes.label: Quality Gate: 59 Tests, Lint, Typecheck Green Every Phase
nodes.norm_label: quality gate: 59 tests, lint, typecheck green every phase
nodes.rationale: The overhaul is sequenced in phases, so each phase must leave the full test/lint/typecheck suite green to keep the refactor landable.

nodes.label: Rollback Policy: Forward Fix, Not Revert to Public Commit
nodes.norm_label: rollback policy: forward fix, not revert to public commit
nodes.rationale: Rolling the app alone back to public commit c9e9592 is unsafe and incompatible with the new settings/required-owner schema, so a forward fix retaining the private guard (or a backup restored into an isolated branch) is preferred.

nodes.label: AI-assisted paste extraction
nodes.rationale: AI only arranges a pasted report into an editable draft; the user reviews every field and the normal form remains the save path, so a bad model output can never write data.

nodes.label: The Meaning Rule
nodes.rationale: Color alone must not carry a result's meaning, so every chart pairs color with legends, units, labels, a tooltip, and a View data table twin; this keeps the charts readable for color-vision-deficient users and when printed.

nodes.label: Reference-led outcome cards
nodes.rationale: Rounded corners and icons are a scoped exception to the square ledger identity so the supplied card reference could be honored without changing surrounding dashboard geometry; the ring shows question shares while its center shows marks/max, never accuracy or a borrowed percentile.

nodes.label: Paper-and-ink visual system
nodes.rationale: Warm editorial paper reading as a printed progress ledger; Anthropic was a visual reference, not a brand to reproduce.

nodes.label: The Readable Table Rule
nodes.rationale: Keep wide tables inside their horizontal scroll container and preserve comparable, nowrap columns instead of squeezing them into unreadable cells.

nodes.label: Private accounts
nodes.rationale: Isolated per-Google-account workspaces with no guest records, shared settings, or administrator views; session failure hides private content so a leaked or stale cookie can never surface another account's data.

nodes.label: Scope boundaries
nodes.rationale: Explicit non-goals (not an exam platform, coaching marketplace, marketing site, or account-management product) keep optional AI an in-app analysis aid rather than an autonomous agent.

nodes.label: Bundled Next.js docs requirement
nodes.rationale: This Next 16 version breaks APIs, conventions, and file layout relative to model training data, so node_modules/next/dist/docs must be read before writing Next.js code.

nodes.label: URL filter and scope mirror
nodes.rationale: Filters and scope are mirrored with history.replaceState so shared links restore the view on load, while Back still changes routes and typing triggers no RSC round-trips.

nodes.label: Next.js 16 constraints
nodes.rationale: App Router with server components by default, no Cache Components, and no shared caching or revalidate on account data because every payload is per-user and personalized.

nodes.label: Ownership from the verified session
nodes.rationale: Ownership is always the verified Neon Auth user ID from requireUser(); a userId from a body, query, or backup is never accepted, so a forged payload cannot reach another account.

nodes.label: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and 503 AUTH_UNAVAILABLE
nodes.rationale: Missing sessions and verification outages get distinct codes so the client can distinguish sign-in-again from retry-later, and neither case returns private records.

nodes.label: Google OAuth setup checklist
nodes.rationale: The Google-authorized redirect URI is the managed Auth callback, not the app's callbackURL, and credentials are configured per Neon branch because each branch has its own Auth base URL.

nodes.label: Backup format v2
nodes.rationale: The file carries attempts, subject results, target, summary, and warnings but no email, userId, or credentials, so it is portable into a different signed-in account without transferring identity.

nodes.label: Import preview fingerprint
nodes.rationale: A SHA-256 fingerprint over destination content, incoming content, both targets, mode, and applyTarget makes a stale preview fail with 409, preventing a commit against data the user never reviewed.

nodes.label: Import merge and replace modes
nodes.rationale: Replace is destructive, so it is never silent: it requires a current safety backup and a confirmation naming the signed-in account.

nodes.label: Migration policy
nodes.rationale: Migrations use the unpooled URL, are applied explicitly after testing on an expiring branch, and never run reset or touch Neon's managed Auth schema, because automatic or pooled migrations can corrupt shared auth data.

nodes.label: AI subsystem
nodes.rationale: AI is optional, read-only, and server-only, and must fail closed without breaking the tracker; only MockForm save creates attempts, so prompt injection cannot write data.

nodes.label: AI context privacy whitelist
nodes.rationale: A whitelist of aggregates, subjects/sections, target, and the latest 20 full mocks, with notes omitted at the Prisma query; anything outside that set is never sent, because an external provider operator can see whatever context is shipped.

nodes.label: AI read-only guarantee
nodes.rationale: AI routes never call repository writes and only MockForm save creates attempts, so prompt-injected instructions in a report or chat message cannot change data.

nodes.label: Extraction draft contract
nodes.rationale: The draft is editable and nullable with evidence and field-level issues rather than raw AttemptInput, keeping missing values distinct from explicit zero and forcing a blocker-free user review before any save.

nodes.label: AI coach insight card
nodes.rationale: Generated manually rather than on page load so an optional, metered external call never fires just from opening the dashboard.

nodes.label: Environment variables
nodes.rationale: Every value stays server-side with no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, and build/client generation never connects to the database or needs live secrets.

nodes.label: HTTP API surface
nodes.rationale: Routes keep {data}/{error} envelopes, same-origin writes, and size limits; type/subject filter Mock history and Compare while dashboard scopes ignore them, and literal substring search escapes PostgreSQL wildcards.

nodes.label: Analytical scopes (full / subject / sectional / all)
nodes.rationale: Tabs change the analytical grain rather than filtering the saved-record table, so one saved attempt can be read at several projections without the user losing the record-level view.

nodes.label: Derived-section isolation
nodes.rationale: Derived sections sum child results and do not inherit the full mock score override, rank, percentile, or overall time; parent-level provenance is meaningless at a narrower grain and would fabricate precision.

nodes.label: Full mock layout 30/30/45/25 = 390
nodes.rationale: Fixed SSC CGL Tier 2 subject counts and a 390 maximum; optional Computer is scored separately and excluded from full totals while its time still counts, so the full-mock total matches the real exam denominator.

nodes.label: No-union invariant for All Mocks
nodes.rationale: Unioning projections would count one full mock again as four subjects and two sections, inflating totals; All Mocks projects each saved parent attempt exactly once.

nodes.label: Section I and Section II derivation
nodes.norm_label: section i and section ii derivation
nodes.rationale: Sections are derived analytics, not database rows, so a full mock always yields exactly one Section I and one Section II point without any stored duplication.

nodes.label: Outcome card ring center semantics
nodes.rationale: Rings encode question shares and the center encodes marks divided by maximum, not accuracy or percentile; a parent full or sectional percentile is never reused for its subject slices or derived sections.

nodes.label: Mock logging workflow
nodes.rationale: Logging must stay quick: scores derive live from question counts, time blocks sum automatically, and empty blocks become zero so the form never blocks on optional detail.

nodes.label: Study planner subsystem
nodes.rationale: Plan is static validated source data and progress is keyed by deterministic identities (taskKey = d{day}:{taskIndex}), so completing work never rewrites the schedule and there is no seed or duplicate-row risk; tracker results and plan results stay deliberately separate stores.

nodes.label: Tracker / plan store separation
nodes.rationale: The tracker keeps full subject-level MockAttempts while plan progress records the plan task's own score/wrong/unattempted fields; merging them would force the read-only schedule and the results ledger into one mutable shape.

nodes.label: Revision queue (Rev-1/Rev-2/Rev-3)
nodes.rationale: Revision completion is always manual; attempting a test never marks its revision done, so the schedule cannot silently drift.

nodes.label: Subject categorical hue mapping
nodes.rationale: A fixed categorical hue order validated for adjacent-pair CVD and normal-vision separation on paper; nominal series are never colored by value or cycled with extra hues, so the same entity keeps its color across filters.

nodes.label: Single percentage axis charts
nodes.rationale: One percentage axis per chart; raw marks stay in tooltips and data tables, so no dual-axis chart can imply a false correlation.

nodes.label: No Zustand and no TanStack Query decision
nodes.community_name: No Zustand and no TanStack Query decision
nodes.norm_label: no zustand and no tanstack query decision
nodes.rationale: The shell never unmounts inside the workspace, so shell-scoped hooks already hold all shared client state and no cross-component sync problem exists for a store to solve; revisit only if genuinely global client state or polling server state appears.

nodes.rationale: Five palettes by three styles resolve entirely through CSS custom properties set before paint, so no component hardcodes palette hexes and all 15 combinations keep AA accent contrast plus identical layout and behavior.

nodes.label: WorkspaceShell Client Orchestrator and Its Three Hooks
nodes.norm_label: workspaceshell client orchestrator and its three hooks
nodes.rationale: State is split into use-workspace-data, use-ai-workspace, and use-backup-import so chat-stream tokens and filter keystrokes do not re-render memo-wrapped charts.

nodes.label: Semantic Chart Palette and Chart Rules
nodes.norm_label: semantic chart palette and chart rules
nodes.rationale: Subject hues are a fixed categorical order validated for CVD and normal-vision separation against paper; series are never colored by value and no extra hues are cycled, so an entity keeps one color across filters. Single percentage axis, animation off, reduced motion respected.

nodes.label: Palettes x Styles Theme Matrix
nodes.rationale: Styles change geometry, density, elevation, and motion but never layout, content, or behavior; semantic positive/warning/danger colors are deliberately not re-tinted per palette so meaning stays stable.

nodes.label: Typography Scale (Source Serif 4 + DM Sans)
nodes.rationale: Serif for headings, metrics, and wordmark; sans for body, tables, forms, navigation; units stay in muted ink rather than reducing their contrast, and tabular figures keep comparison values aligned.

nodes.label: dashboard.tsx Monolith Split Finding
nodes.rationale: One 1721-line file mixed shell, settings, history, compare, and dialogs, and the api() fetch helper lived in mock-form.tsx (wrong boundary), so both had to be separated before component work could proceed.

nodes.label: UI Baseline Audit Findings (26 prioritized items)
nodes.norm_label: ui baseline audit findings (26 prioritized items)

nodes.label: 15-Phase Execution Order
nodes.rationale: Tokens before shell before pages before components-in-pages, with all 59 tests, lint, and typecheck kept green after every phase, so later phases never build on unsound tokens.

nodes.label: Missing Radius System Finding
nodes.rationale: DESIGN.md mandates square corners but reality was mixed (rounded-2xl maintenance page, 10px outcome cards, 4px skeletons, pill landing tiles) with no tokens, so the 'moderately rounded corners' directive had to be satisfied by a tokenized radius scale on controls rather than by rounding structural geometry.

nodes.label: Elevation Model and --shadow-pop Token
nodes.rationale: Depth is flat at level 0 via rules and surface change; the single lifted token is ink-tinted (never gray-on-cream) and reserved for popovers, toasts, dialogs, and command surfaces, with hover lift done by rule darkening plus 2px translate instead of shadows.

nodes.label: Restrained Motion Language
nodes.rationale: 140ms hover, 220ms enter, 240ms view switch with no horizontal slides, 70ms stagger capped at 6 children and only once; charts never animate and every new path must be reduced-motion aware.

nodes.label: Tokenized Radius Scale (panel/control/card/pill)
nodes.rationale: 0px for panels/stat strip/tables/dialogs/nav preserves the ledger identity, 4px belongs to controls, 10px to expressive cards, and pills only to dots and bars — tokens rather than per-component guesswork.

nodes.label: Accessibility Pass (skip link, focus, aria)
nodes.rationale: The skip link now moves real focus into <main tabIndex={-1}> rather than only scrolling; color is never the sole signal because values are printed alongside status colors.

nodes.label: Unified Segmented Control (.segment-group)
nodes.rationale: Replaced three ad-hoc treatments (scope tabs, entry mode, import mode) with one pattern that wraps instead of clipping at <=420px and exposes aria-pressed/role=group.

nodes.label: Sticky Identity Column for Mock History
nodes.norm_label: sticky identity column for mock history
nodes.rationale: At 375px the ledger's remaining columns scroll while the mock name stays pinned, so a row stays identifiable; verified by scrolling 220px.

nodes.label: Dashboard Scope Projection Invariants
nodes.rationale: Tabs are analytical scopes, not record filters: never union projections for All Mocks (one full mock must not recount as four subjects and two sections), derived sections never inherit the parent's override/rank/percentile/time, and missing values stay null rather than zero.

nodes.label: Paper-and-Ink Design System
nodes.rationale: Warm editorial paper (cream canvas, paper surfaces, serif headings, terracotta actions, thin rules) chosen for the clarity of a printed progress ledger; Anthropic was a visual reference, not a brand identity to reproduce.

nodes.label: Handover Conventions to Keep
nodes.rationale: Identity is the ledger (structural geometry square, 4px controls, 10px expressive cards), one segmented-control pattern, all icons through icon.tsx, semantic accuracy color always paired with the printed value, deployment-neutral copy — so future features cannot erode the overhaul.

nodes.label: "The Printed Progress Ledger" Design Direction
nodes.rationale: Product personality is a calm editorial workspace treating exam prep as a record worth keeping: every addition must feel typeset, not decorated, which is why structural geometry stays square and palette/chart hues are frozen.

nodes.label: Backup Format v2 and Account Transfer
nodes.norm_label: backup format v2 and account transfer
nodes.rationale: Fingerprint-gated, transactional merge/replace exist so a stale preview cannot commit; replace is double-gated (client safety download naming the account, server confirmReplace) because destructive replacement must never be silent.

nodes.label: Request and Ownership Architecture
nodes.rationale: Ownership is always the verified Neon Auth user ID from requireUser(); a userId from body, query, or backup is never accepted, and foreign vs nonexistent IDs both return 404 so ID probing reveals nothing.

nodes.label: Neon Agent Tooling Setup (Codex plugin + MCP)
nodes.norm_label: neon agent tooling setup (codex plugin + mcp)
nodes.rationale: The bundled neon-postgres plugin already ships the Neon skills and the OAuth MCP server, so no duplicate standalone skills/MCP entries were added; CLI operations were preferred, and a failed unrelated Copilot installer was bypassed with --agent codex.

nodes.label: Expiring QA Branch Migration Rehearsal
nodes.rationale: The reviewed initial migration ran on an expiring branch first and only then on production, so a broken migration could not damage real data.

nodes.label: Private-Accounts Migration (claim two shared mocks)
nodes.rationale: The migration only targets ssc_insight, reads the managed Auth table to find exactly one email-verified identity, aborts on any unexpected nonzero mock count, and never claims records for the first visitor.

nodes.label: Session-Derived Ownership Model
nodes.rationale: Every data route verifies Neon Auth independently and bypasses the SDK's five-minute cookie cache so revoked sessions cannot authorize requests, even though that costs a verification call per request.

nodes.label: JSON Backup Format Version 2
nodes.rationale: The 4 MB / 10,000-attempt cap exists to stay inside the deployment request-body limit; backups are manual only (no scheduled jobs, reminders, email, or ZIP) by product decision, and CSV stays read-only because only the versioned JSON has a lossless round-trip contract.

nodes.label: Google Sign-In via Neon Auth OAuth
nodes.norm_label: google sign-in via neon auth oauth
nodes.rationale: The callback registered with Google is {NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL}/callback/google, not the app's /auth/complete landing, and each branch has its own Auth base URL — a common setup mistake. Server-side requireUser() is authoritative; client useSession() is only a UI fallback.

nodes.label: Verification Scripts and QA Discipline
nodes.rationale: A passing session endpoint is not proof of Google login, and destructive replace checks are gated behind ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_REPLACE because they run against real disposable accounts on a QA branch.

nodes.label: Three Date Semantics (scheduled / attempt / recorded)
nodes.rationale: Scheduled date = plan day, attempt date = completedAt (used by filters, ordering, analytics), recorded date = createdAt shown only as 'Logged'; trend ordering uses completedAt so a late-logged mock still plots on its real attempt date.

nodes.label: Controlled Release and Rollback Strategy
nodes.rationale: Rolling the app alone back to the public revision is unsafe and schema-incompatible, so a forward fix keeping the private guard is preferred; any destructive production restore needs a new reviewed release that preserves later private-account records.

nodes.label: Product Principles (quick logging, readable analysis)
nodes.rationale: Keep logging quick and analysis readable; uses calm direct language, warm paper with editorial typography, IST dates, and scores whose underlying meaning survives across differing mock maxima.

nodes.label: Generated Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: Written and re-added by `next dev` via generate-agent-files.js; requires reading bundled Next 16 docs before writing code, and removing it from a diff only recreates the uncommitted change, so it should be committed with the work.

nodes.label: Per-User Encrypted AI Credentials
nodes.rationale: User credential wins over server env and drives quota source; keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted into aiKeyEnc, never returned (only a 4-char hint), never backed up, and a rotated secret degrades rows to 'not configured' rather than erroring.

nodes.label: SSRF Guard for User-Controlled AI Base URL
nodes.norm_label: ssrf guard for user-controlled ai base url
nodes.rationale: Because the base URL is user-controlled, loopback/RFC1918/link-local/metadata/CGNAT/multicast/reserved ranges are blocked and DNS is re-resolved immediately before every provider call; save-time shape validation alone cannot see host -> 10.0.0.5. Residual DNS-rebinding risk is documented, not claimed solved.

nodes.label: Vercel Configuration Preparation
nodes.rationale: Secrets were passed over stdin and never printed or committed; the previous environment export cannot fully restore sensitive values because Vercel substitutes placeholders, so the old variables were left intact rather than replaced.

nodes.label: Known Limitations (duo-icons fill-rule, native inputs)
nodes.rationale: Native selects and date inputs keep platform UI deliberately for touch reliability; the duo-icons fill-rule warning is library-internal and the Recharts 0-size warning is dev-only, so neither justifies churn.

nodes.label: Icon Size Scale (14/16/18/22/28)
nodes.rationale: Duo icons first with Lucide fallback and no ad-hoc sizes; icon-only controls always carry aria-label and decorative icons aria-hidden.

nodes.label: Named Imports for Bundle Reduction
nodes.rationale: A namespace import from @duo-icons/react kept unused glyphs in the client bundle; per-glyph named imports funnel every icon through icon.tsx so unused ones drop out.

nodes.label: Raw Lucide Imports Migrated into Semantic Icon Map
nodes.norm_label: raw lucide imports migrated into semantic icon map
nodes.rationale: The maintenance page keeps an intentionally inlined server-side icon to avoid shipping client JS for it, and the canonical 14/16/18/22/28 scale holds wherever icons appear.

nodes.label: In-Process Settings LRU Cache
nodes.community_name: No Zustand and no TanStack Query decision
nodes.rationale: The only server-side cache because settings are the only read-hot, rarely-changing, write-through-invalidatable store; accepted cost is a <=60s lag in a second tab and a per-process scope that would need shared storage across instances.

nodes.label: Opt-In SWR Headers for Non-App Consumers
nodes.community_name: No Zustand and no TanStack Query decision
nodes.norm_label: opt-in swr headers for non-app consumers
nodes.rationale: The app client sends cache: no-store, so max-age/stale-while-revalidate exists only for QA scripts and future prefetch; raising them would speed scripts but risk post-mutation staleness in charts, so correctness wins.

nodes.label: URL State Mirror (filters/scope in address bar)
nodes.community_name: No Zustand and no TanStack Query decision
nodes.norm_label: url state mirror (filters/scope in address bar)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly not a cache: history.replaceState mirrors filters so shared links reload the same view without an RSC round-trip per keystroke.

nodes.label: Conservative Caching Policy (private by default)
nodes.community_name: No Zustand and no TanStack Query decision
nodes.rationale: Every workspace payload is personalized, so nothing user-specific is shared and anything that must reflect a mutation immediately is not cached at all; this document is the authoritative matrix (Phase 8 of the 2026-10 architecture overhaul) and must be updated before any policy change.
